clue.text: Drone in America having completed miles

parts.note: THRU is the American spelling of 'through', meaning finished or completed

explanation.surface: A sound or a worker bee in the USA, having travelled a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in America' tells you to use the American spelling THRU for 'through' (finished).
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming sound, the same as a drone.

clue.text: Disconcerted as a result of broadcast getting cancelled

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: through means owing to, as in 'lost through carelessness'
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: Upset because a radio programme was called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that THROUGH (as a result of) is heard, giving THREW; then OFF for cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown off is being put off one's stride, flustered or disconcerted.

clue.text: Arm muscle — it turns in both directions

indicators.note: in both directions says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: something that turns or spins can be called by this name

explanation.surface: A muscle of the arm that can twist both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTATOR is a palindrome, and the word literally means a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotator cuff muscles in the shoulder turn the upper arm.

clue.text: Film takes against leading supporter of the royals

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, of water droplets for example
on means against, as in leaning on a wall
arch means leading or chief, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: A film is taken against a prominent royalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchist backs a monarchy and so supports the royal family.

clue.text: In spite of everything, they're oddly entering a decline

indicators.note: entering says these letters go inside the phrase for 'a decline'

parts.note: a fall is a decline or drop

indicators.note: oddly says to take the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of they're

explanation.surface: Despite everything, some people are sinking into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of they're, and 'entering' puts them inside the phrase for 'a decline'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless, when everything is considered.

clue.text: Hero flounders badly, carrying unknown injury

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the extra letter goes within
badly says the letters are put into a poor, mixed-up order

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns, so Z

explanation.surface: A hero struggles awkwardly while hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen shoulder is a painful stiffening of the shoulder joint, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Former leader of East Germany with English name

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A past East German leader with an English name.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a past British prime minister, so a political chief of old.

clue.text: Device for connecting plug, suitable in the place of missing lead

parts.note: a plug is an advert, AD for short
apt means suitable

indicators.note: missing lead says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: for means in place of, as in 'swap this for that'

explanation.surface: An electrical gadget fits a plug when its lead has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' looks part of the definition but is the advert, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor lets one piece of equipment link to another of a different type.

clue.text: Bug requiring computers, etc. to be taken out of service

indicators.note: to be taken out of says one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: a liturgy is a form of church service
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

explanation.surface: A software bug means computers must be shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy is jokey British slang for an unspecified illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is a minor illness, and so is the lurgy in British slang.

clue.text: Proposal retained common ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A shared piece of land was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common ground' reads as a phrase, but 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A recommendation is a suggestion put forward, a proposal.

clue.text: Train carriage's rear section withdrawn by engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters are read in reverse
rear says to take the final letter of the word carriage

parts.note: a unit is a section, for example of an army

explanation.surface: Railway engineers have taken the back part of a train carriage out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns round the carriage's last letter together with the section, giving TINUE. Train here means a retinue, not a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a group of attendants following an important person, which is a retinue.

clue.text: Old couple grabbing small space outside

indicators.note: grabbing says one piece takes hold of another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a pair is a couple
an en is a small space in printing, half an em

explanation.surface: An elderly couple squeeze into a tiny room outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-air takes place outdoors rather than inside a building.

clue.text: Sadly, owls nearly starve without primarily eating rodents

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next letter
sadly signals that the letters are put into a sorry, jumbled state
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of owls is dropped
primarily means first, so take the opening letter of eating

explanation.surface: Hungry owls are unhappily going without their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' gives OWL; 'Sadly' scrambles OWL plus STARVE, and 'without' (outside) puts that round E, from 'primarily eating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water voles are small riverbank rodents found in Britain, like the character Ratty.

clue.text: Guy, for example, takes time

indicators.note: takes means accepts inside, so the time letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: Someone called Guy, say, is taking his time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guy here is not a man but a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope holding a tent or mast steady, and so is a stay.

clue.text: A quiet dance introduces each show

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: introduces means brings inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to prance is to dance or caper

explanation.surface: A soft dance opens each performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an appearance is to show up, so appearance is a showing.

clue.text: Team sport organised alongside river, generally

indicators.note: alongside says the river is set next to the rearranged letters

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: organised says the letters of team sport are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports team gets itself together by a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning mostly or usually, the same as generally.

clue.text: Concern among all other people leaving hospital

parts.note: in means among, as in 'in the crowd'

indicators.note: leaving says this letter departs from the phrase

parts.note: the rest means everyone else

explanation.surface: Worry spreads among everyone else as they leave hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a stake or business involvement, a concern.

clue.text: Involving two individuals: a boy in contact with a boy

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
a son is a boy
to means touching, as in 'face to face'
per means a, as in 'twice a day'
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Two lads are touching each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A person-to-person call or meeting is directly between two people.

clue.text: People bragged occasionally about new table ornament

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go round the next
occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Folk sometimes boasted about a fancy new centrepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes EPERGE from the even letters of People bragged; 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, often with dishes.

clue.text: Last three pieces of fresh lamb prepared for butcher's stand

indicators.note: prepared says the letters are made ready in a new form
the last three pieces means the final three letters of the next word

explanation.surface: The final cuts of fresh lamb are made ready for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last three pieces of' gives ESH from fresh; 'prepared' scrambles ESH plus LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamble is an old word for a meat stall, hence shambles for a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Rissole obviously contains fat

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held within the words before it

explanation.surface: A fried meat cake is clearly greasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleo is short for oleomargarine, a cooking fat, and a crossword staple.

clue.text: Have untold pride in the first instance and confess

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: in the first instance means at the start, so the opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: Have enormous pride at first, then admit it.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom meaning to admit a fault, to confess.

clue.text: Personalised trial arranged with a demo

indicators.note: arranged says these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A custom trial is set up, along with a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailor-made means made to suit one particular person's needs.

clue.text: Nothing works. My bad!

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
OPS is short for opuses, musical works

explanation.surface: Nothing works: sorry, my mistake!
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual exclamations admitting a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Knock back some gin (or generous cocktail that requires it!)

indicators.note: Knock back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Down some gin, or a generous cocktail that needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is the gin just mentioned: the cocktail needs gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Negroni is a cocktail of gin, vermouth and Campari, so it needs gin.

clue.text: European knights boasted endlessly about love and honour

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight, so two knights give NN
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: blew, as in blew one's own trumpet, means boasted

explanation.surface: European knights bragged on and on about love and honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just joins the pieces here: E, NN, O, then BLE(W).
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to honour them, literally by raising them to the nobility.

clue.text: Acceptable excuses given by worker?

parts.note: pleas are excuses offered in defence
an ant is a worker, in crosswords the usual insect worker

explanation.surface: Is a worker's excuse good enough?
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant is agreeable, so acceptable in the sense of welcome.

clue.text: Leave old food unfinished

parts.note: ex means former, so old

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter is removed

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Leave the stale food uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission for a pupil or student to be absent, a leave of absence.
